info.title: Paper Trading Challenge API
info.description: Backend for a paper trading competition. Tags mirror the brief's seven required operations. Money and prices are decimal **strings** at four decimal places — never JSON numbers — and errors are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` carrying the numbers that explain them.

get.summary: The journal, narrated — every event as a human sentence
get.description: Not a second log: this IS the event log, read back with words on. Pass ?after=<seq> to fetch incrementally (the cockpit polls this with its last-seen seq, which is how anything you do here in Swagger appears in the cockpit's Journal within two seconds).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events with seq strictly greater than this

post.summary: Operator reset: destroy the world, restore the boot state
post.description: Destructive and deliberate. Empties the event log, rebirths the engine and the broker (fresh RNG stream and id counters — a reset world is exactly as deterministic as a rebooted one), and re-applies the instrument seeds as fresh journalled events. The log is append-only *within* a competition; the competition itself is the operator's to discard. Beyond the brief: this is the paper system's demo-account reset.

200.description: Counts of participants, orders, events and closed days

post.summary: Create a participant with starting cash

get.summary: Cash, positions, average price, realized/unrealized P&L, fees, total value, active orders
get.description: If a held symbol has no mark, the read still succeeds with `totalValue: null` and a `valuationError` naming the symbol — fail closed means never a wrong number, not never a response.

get.summary: Full order history for one participant

post.summary: Submit an order (the server mints the order id)
post.description: Pre-trade checks reserve against **working** orders: available cash = balance − Σ(remaining notional + fee) of open buys, so two orders cannot spend the same cash. Rejected inputs are never repaired: `10.123456`, `aapl`, side `BUY` are all 400s.

422.description: Insufficient available cash or position — the body carries the numbers

example.title: insufficient cash
example.detail: insufficient available cash: need 300.1500, 99.5500 free after working orders

delete.summary: Cancel a working order — filled quantity survives

409.description: Illegal transition — the body names the current state

example.title: illegal transition
example.detail: cannot apply a cancellation to an order in state FILLED

put.summary: Cancel-replace: new terms, new order, chained via `replaces`
put.description: Returns **both** sides — the original CANCELLED with its fills intact, and the replacement working at the new terms (FIX OrigClOrdID semantics).

409.description: Terminal order, or replacement id already used

get.summary: The trade blotter for one order
get.description: Every execution booked against the order, each with the venue's ExecID (FIX tag 17) — cloid names the intent, the ack carried the oid, and each fill carries its tid. In production the ExecID is the dedup key for redelivered reports; here every operator command mints a fresh one because the operator is the venue.

get.summary: The tape — every execution in the world, ExecID order
get.description: One row per fill, keyed by execId (FIX ExecID 17): the brokerOrderId names the order at the venue and is shared by all its fills, so the blotter keys on the id that names each fill. Every row carries the full trio — execId, clientOrderId, brokerOrderId — plus participant, symbol, side, qty, px, fee.

200.description: { executions: [{execId, clientOrderId, brokerOrderId, participant, symbol, side, qty, px, fee}] }

post.summary: Generate an execution report for a working order
post.description: Send `qty` **and** `px` to dictate the terms (the deterministic-test path), or **neither** to let the seeded broker slice — each auto execution takes at least 1/max_slices of the order. Exactly one of the pair is a 400: refused, not half-guessed.

409.description: Order is terminal, or nothing remains to execute

422.description: Overfill, empty fill, or the book refuses the fill

get.summary: The security master — every listed instrument and its grids
get.description: FIX would call this a SecurityList. An **empty list means unrestricted**: any well-formed symbol trades on permissive grids (tick 0.0001, lot 1). Once anything is listed, the venue is an allowlist and off-list or off-grid orders come back as recorded REJECTED orders with a precise reason (UnknownSymbol, PriceOffTick, QtyOffLot, ExceedsSizeLimit). Ask first; don't discover by rejection.

post.description: The first listing switches the venue from unrestricted to allowlist mode. Journalled like everything else — the registry is event-sourced state, and replay rebuilds it.

put.description: Working orders were judged against the spec at submission and are not retroactively re-checked — the venue changed its rules; it did not unwind your order.

delete.description: Refused with the counts while any working order or open position references the symbol — delisting must not strand what it cannot unwind.

409.description: In use — body carries workingOrders and positions counts

post.summary: Update marks (batch) — this is the market moving
post.description: Every entry is parsed before any is applied: a batch with one malformed price updates nothing.

post.summary: Close a trading day and publish its leaderboard
post.description: Idempotent — re-closing returns the published board even if marks moved since. Days close in order. Fails closed (409) if any held symbol lacks a mark: a wrong closing value would corrupt an immutable board.

409.description: Missing mark, or day out of order — body names which

get.description: The payload states its own rules: rankedBy `dailyReturn descending`, tiebreaks `turnover ascending` then `participantId ascending`.
Geometric compound of daily returns. Participants with no active day are listed with `rank: null, eligible: false` — never traded, never placed.

OrderId.name: clientOrderId
OrderId.description: The client order id — FIX ClOrdID (11), minted by the server at submit. Not the broker's OrderID (37), which appears as brokerOrderId in responses.

BadRequest.description: Rejected input — strict parsing, nothing repaired

InstrumentSpec.description: The security master's row: the grids an order must sit on

tick.description: Minimum price increment; finest legal is 0.0001

Money.description: Decimal string, four places, exact — never a JSON number

symbol.description: Upper-case only — `aapl` is rejected, not normalised

clientOrderId.description: The id from your submit response — FIX ClOrdID (11)

qty.description: With px: dictate the terms. Omit both for the seeded broker.

OrderView.description: Every id is labelled by its FIX role: clientOrderId (ClOrdID 11, ours), brokerOrderId (OrderID 37, the venue's order), and each fill carries execId (ExecID 17). Nothing is called plain orderId — in FIX that means the broker's id, and ambiguity here is how fills get booked against the wrong order.

brokerOrderId.description: FIX OrderID (37). Null only when the venue never assigned one (pre-ack NEW, REJECTED); once assigned it never disappears

replaces.description: FIX OrigClOrdID — the order this one replaced

Problem.description: RFC 7807, plus domain members carrying the numbers that explain the refusal
